items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: And you know of course then I got turned on to Charlie Parker and the usual.

ctx.x: Yeah, there was a certain sound to that group. I had an experience of just hearing “Take Five” one day on the car radio, and I said, “Man that’s it. What is that?” That kind of starts a whole process maybe of going from one thing to the next.

Right. Exactly. And you know of course then I got turned on to Charlie Parker and the usual. I kept going forward and backwards, forward — every time I ran out of inspiration I would go back. And then I’d run out of that and I’d jump forward and listen to some new guys, and back and forth, back and forth. But every once in a while, there’s old Paul sitting there. I just recently recorded an album with a 51 piece orchestra, the Metropole Orchestra in Holland. And I did a version of “East of the Sun.” And in the…
That’s great — all those years later.
